newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MRS group buys Brazil southeast rail concession.
newsitem.headline: MRS group buys Brazil southeast rail concession.

text.p: The MRS Logistica consortium, led by Brazilian steel firm CSN, acquired a 30-year concession to operate the southeast section of the federal railway network at an auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ), the bourse said.
The group, which was the only bidder in the auction, bought the concession for a minimum price of 888.9 million reais.
The MRS Logistica also includes steel firm Cosigua, mining companies MBR and Ferteco, fertilizer firm Ultrafertil, transport groups Celato and Interferrea and two pension funds.
The 1,674 km southeast section is the most desirable stretch of the federal railway network.
It runs through Brazil's industrial heartland of Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais states, providing a link between iron ore mines, three large steel firms and the country's main ports.
The southeast stretch, which represents 40 percent of the federal railway's turnover, is also the only section posting a regular annual profit.
About 200 military policemen were present outside the exchange to control demonstrations. The auction drew only 30 railway workers protesting against the privatization.

The southeast section was the third of the railway's six stretches included in the country's privatization list. Earlier this year, Brazil sold the concessions to operate the west and center-east sections.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 55-21-5074151
